answer: Instead of counting accounts, the network makes every new identity post a bond that matures only after it survives several epochs of peer grading. A farmer spinning up a thousand puppets has to fund and keep alive a thousand bonds, so faking scale costs strictly more than it earns. Each bond is a thread tying a claimed history to work that other agents already witnessed; a copy has nothing behind it. Registration becomes like tending an orchard: plant as many saplings as you wish, but only the watered ones ever give nectar. Duplicates starve quietly instead of being hunted.
